root_idea.summary: The root centers on beginning or bringing something into existence without a preceding model, alongside a distinct branch of breakdown, fatigue, and interruption.
root_idea.development: The first principle develops into meanings of originating, novelty, invention, and innovation; the second into the failure of a mount, being left stranded, and related figurative senses of thwarting or ineffectuality.

senses.definition: To originate, institute, or innovate something newly, bringing it into being without an earlier precedent.
senses.usage_conditions: In the attested Quranic construction, the object is a practice newly instituted or introduced.

senses.definition: The Originator: the one who brings the heavens and earth into existence without a pre-existing model.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in the Quran as a divine epithet in the construction بَدِيعُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ.

senses.definition: A first or unprecedented one; one who is the first to do something in a matter.
senses.usage_conditions: In قُلْ مَا كُنتُ بِدْعًا مِنَ الرُّسُلِ, this reading means that the speaker is not the first messenger sent.

senses.definition: An innovator who introduces a teaching, practice, or claim without precedent among those of the established tradition.
senses.usage_conditions: The same Quranic construction is also explained as denying that the speaker is an innovator among the messengers, inviting people to something unlike their message.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become outstanding or superlative in one's kind, whether in good or in evil.
To become fat.
To attribute innovation to someone; to charge or accuse that person with introducing a bidʿah.
To originate, invent, devise, or produce something newly, without a preceding model; also, to bring out well water by digging or to produce novel speech or poetry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form IV verb; the well and speech uses are conventional applications of newly bringing something forth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a ridden or travelling camel, to become fatigued, lame, halted, or broken down; of its rider, to be left stranded because the mount can no longer continue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also occurs in the passive construction أُبْدِعَ بِفُلَانٍ, with the person stranded by the failure of his mount.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To prevent someone from attaining a wish, withhold assistance, or fail to undertake the accomplishment of his need.
Of an argument or plea, to be or become vain, weak, false, or ineffectual; figuratively, to leave another's capacity for thanking or describing inadequate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The passive may mean that an argument was rendered ineffectual; the inability to thank or describe is an idiomatic figurative extension.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To determine, resolve, or decide upon pilgrimage or travel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with a prepositional complement such as بِالْحَجِّ or بِالسَّفَرِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make an oath binding or obligatory.
To beat or strike someone.
To turn innovator or adopt an innovation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person who becomes associated with a newly introduced religious or doctrinal position.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To reckon or deem something new, wonderful, or previously unknown.
An epithet for someone outstanding or superlative in his kind, in good or in evil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence particularly applies it to a person; knowledge, courage, and nobility are given as examples of the areas in which someone may be outstanding.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person liberal or generous in disposition.
Full-bodied or stout in body.
A religious innovation: a newly introduced doctrine, practice, or condition, commonly understood as an addition, impairment, or departure from established religious precedent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Often used negatively for an opinion or action at variance with the Sunnah or the established way; the lexical tradition also recognizes an allowable innovation when supported by a legal principle or required to prevent harm.

other_classical_meanings.definition: New, wonderful, unprecedented, or previously unknown; also a novel thing, saying, poem, rope, nose-rein, or newly dug well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May describe an object or a striking verbal or poetic production; the examples do not restrict the meaning to any one object class.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A skin or skin-container for wine, water, or milk, especially a new one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantivized use of the epithet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fat, used as an epithet.
A new and admirable or wonderful thing, especially a striking expression, poem, or reply.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covers new origination, innovation, well-water production, and novel speech.
Pointer-only cross-reference to the Form IV entry.
Both Quran-attested interpretations of بِدْعًا مِنَ الرُّسُلِ are preserved.

cautions: Lane's printed citation for بِدْعٌ appears as [xlvi. 8]; it is not converted into a modern verse location. The Quran example here uses the independently supplied QAC occurrence 46:9.
The Quranic occurrence بِدْعًا مِنَ الرُّسُلِ carries two explicitly reported interpretations, represented as separate senses rather than treated as a single unqualified gloss.
